description: Dashboard trail: color the trail (connectors/path between nodes and the active section) based on the CURRENT/selected module's color, with a fallback to var(--brand-purple) when a module has no color; and ensure the SELECTED node is always centered horizontally in the viewport, both when a node/module is clicked and when the carousel changes the focused module, without breaking pointer-drag or wheel scrolling. Frontend only (modules.color already exists in schema and is already selected by useCourseTrail). This feature is independent of FEAT-003.
steps: Trail coloring - data/current-module: In src/features/dashboard/DashboardPage.tsx the trail already tracks focusedModuleId and renders TrailTrack. Determine the 'current module' as the focused module (focusedModuleId) when set, else default to the first module of the trail. Compute its color (module.color ?? 'var(--brand-purple)'). Default focusedModuleId to the first module when the trail loads/changes (add an effect that sets focusedModuleId to trail.modules[0].module.id when focusedModuleId is null or no longer present in the current trail), so the trail always has a current color even before the user interacts.

Trail coloring - render: Make the trail connectors/path reflect the current module color. Today there are NO connector lines in .dash__track (nodes are just laid out with flex gap). Add a visible connecting path/segment between nodes and color it with the current module's color. Implement by passing the current color into TrailTrack and exposing it to CSS via a CSS custom property on the trail/track container (e.g. set style={{ ['--trail-color' as string]: currentColor }} on the .dash__track or .dash__trail element) and add CSS in src/styles/theme.css that draws connector segments (e.g. a horizontal line via a ::before/::after or a dedicated connector element between modules/lessons) using var(--trail-color). Per-module segments MAY use each module's own color for its own sub-section; at minimum the overall active path and the current section must use the current/selected module color. Keep the module-node background and lesson 'available' accent consistent with this (the module node already uses m.module.color). Ensure the fallback var(--brand-purple) is used when color is null.

Also reflect the current color on the carousel's active item if it is not already (dash__carousel-item--active currently uses var(--brand-purple)); use the focused module's color for the active carousel pill so the UI is consistent. Keep borderColor per item = m.module.color ?? var(--brand-purple) as today.

Centering - extract pure math: Add a small pure helper (e.g. src/features/dashboard/helpers.ts, exported function such as computeCenterScrollLeft({ containerWidth, nodeOffsetLeft, nodeWidth, maxScrollLeft }) => number) that returns the scrollLeft needed to center a node horizontally: nodeOffsetLeft + nodeWidth/2 - containerWidth/2, clamped to [0, maxScrollLeft]. This is unit-testable without a DOM.

Centering - wire it: Rewrite scrollToModule(moduleId) in DashboardPage.tsx so that instead of el.scrollIntoView({ inline: 'start' }) it centers the module node horizontally within the trail container (trailRef). Use the trail container (trailRef.current) scroll metrics: containerWidth = trailRef.current.clientWidth, the node element's offsetLeft relative to the scroll container (prefer node.offsetLeft; if the node is not a direct offsetParent child, compute via getBoundingClientRect offsets relative to the container), nodeWidth = node.offsetWidth, maxScrollLeft = scrollWidth - clientWidth. Set trailRef.current.scrollTo({ left: computeCenterScrollLeft(...), behavior: 'smooth' }). Apply this on carousel click (scrollToModule) AND when focusedModuleId changes programmatically. Keep setFocusedModuleId in scrollToModule.

Centering on node click: when a lesson or module node is clicked/selected in the trail, also center it (set the focused module and center on that module). At minimum, keep the carousel-driven centering working; if lesson clicks navigate away (onOpenLesson), centering the owning module on focus-change is sufficient. Do not add centering logic that fights the user's active drag (only auto-center on explicit selection/carousel/focus changes, never during pointer drag).

Preserve drag/wheel: Do NOT change the behavior of useHorizontalDragScroll.ts beyond what is necessary. The container must remain overflow-x: auto and the drag/wheel handlers must keep working. Verify that centering uses the same scroll container the drag handlers mutate (trailRef) so they do not conflict.

Tests: Add/extend a vitest unit test (src/features/dashboard/__tests__/helpers.test.ts or a new co-located test) covering computeCenterScrollLeft: node in the middle centers correctly, node near the start clamps to 0, node near the end clamps to maxScrollLeft, and nodeWidth is accounted for. Also add a tiny pure helper + test for 'current module color resolution' if you extract one (module with color returns it; module with null color returns the brand fallback).
acceptance_criteria: The trail shows a visible connecting path/segments between nodes whose color reflects the current/selected module's color, falling back to var(--brand-purple) when the module color is null.
Selecting a module via the bottom carousel scrolls the trail so that module's node is horizontally centered in the viewport (not snapped to the left edge).
Changing the focused module programmatically (carousel/selection) re-centers the newly focused node.
Pointer-drag and mouse-wheel horizontal scrolling of the trail still work (not broken by the centering change).
computeCenterScrollLeft is a pure exported function with unit tests covering middle, start-clamp, and end-clamp cases; `npm test` passes.
npm run typecheck, npm run lint (no NEW warnings beyond the recorded baseline), and npm run build all pass.
verification: npm test  (new centering helper tests pass)
npm run lint  (no new warnings beyond baseline)
findings_review_round2:
v1 REVIEW FOLLOW-UP - trailRef / centering-origin note. INVESTIGATED and the measurement was already CORRECT, but made ROBUST. Finding: trailRef is attached to .dash__trail (the scroll container; position:absolute, overflow-x:auto). The focused node is .dash__module (which has position:relative and the data-module-id). The review assumed .dash__track gained position:relative, but it did NOT - there is no `position: relative` anywhere in src/styles/theme.css (confirmed by grep). Therefore the nearest POSITIONED ancestor of .dash__module is .dash__trail itself (the only positioned ancestor), which is exactly the scroll container, so node.offsetLeft already shared an origin with container.scrollLeft/clientWidth and centering was accurate. However this correctness was incidental (it relies on .dash__track staying static). FIX: the centering effect in DashboardPage.tsx now measures the node's left edge relative to the scroll container via getBoundingClientRect() + container.scrollLeft (nodeOffsetLeft = nodeRect.left - containerRect.left + container.scrollLeft) and uses nodeRect.width, instead of node.offsetLeft/offsetWidth. This is independent of which ancestor is the offset parent, so centering stays correct even if .dash__track (or any wrapper) is later positioned. computeCenterScrollLeft and its 5 unit tests are unchanged (pure math still correct). Verification after the change: typecheck exit 0, 131 tests pass, lint 6 baseline warnings, build exit 0, prettier clean.

findings:
Frontend-only change, no backend/migration touched (modules.color already selected by useCourseTrail).

Files changed:
- src/features/dashboard/helpers.ts: added two pure helpers. computeCenterScrollLeft({containerWidth, nodeOffsetLeft, nodeWidth, maxScrollLeft}) returns nodeOffsetLeft + nodeWidth/2 - containerWidth/2 clamped to [0, max(0, maxScrollLeft)]. resolveModuleColor(color) returns color ?? 'var(--brand-purple)' (exported TRAIL_FALLBACK_COLOR constant).
- src/features/dashboard/__tests__/helpers.test.ts: added vitest suites for computeCenterScrollLeft (middle centers, start clamps to 0, end clamps to maxScrollLeft, node width accounted for, negative maxScrollLeft -> 0) and resolveModuleColor (color passthrough, null/undefined -> brand fallback). 14 dashboard tests pass; 119 total.
- src/features/dashboard/DashboardPage.tsx: current module = focused module when set else trail.modules[0]; currentColor = resolveModuleColor(currentModule.color). Added effect to default/recover focusedModuleId to trail.modules[0].module.id when null or no longer present in the current trail (so there is always a current color). Rewrote scrollToModule to only setFocusedModuleId; centering moved into an effect keyed on [focusedModuleId, trail] that reads trailRef.current (the SAME scroll container the drag/wheel handlers mutate), computes node.offsetLeft/offsetWidth + container.clientWidth/scrollWidth, and calls container.scrollTo({left: computeCenterScrollLeft(...), behavior:'smooth'}). This replaces the old el.scrollIntoView({inline:'start'}) left-snap. Centering only fires on explicit focus changes (carousel/selection/default), never during drag. TrailTrack now receives currentColor + focusedModuleId; sets style --trail-color on .dash__track and --module-color per .dash__module; active module gets dash__module--active. Carousel active pill now uses the focused module's own color inline (background = resolveModuleColor(m.module.color)); per-item borderColor kept = resolveModuleColor(m.module.color).
- src/styles/theme.css: added connector segments (there were none before - just flex gap). .dash__module::before draws a horizontal connector line colored with var(--trail-color, var(--brand-purple)) (hidden on first-child, full opacity on --active); .dash__lessons::before draws a module->lessons connector colored with var(--module-color, var(--trail-color, var(--brand-purple))) (hidden when lessons empty). .dash__carousel-item--active keeps var(--brand-purple) as CSS fallback while inline background supplies the focused module color.

Drag/wheel: useHorizontalDragScroll.ts left unchanged; centering uses the same trailRef container so no conflict.

Verification (PATH exported to node v22.23.3): npm run typecheck exit 0; npm test 119 passed (9 files); npm run lint 6 warnings 0 errors (unchanged baseline in Toast/AuthProvider/LessonView/QuestionComponents/NotebookPage, none in touched files); npm run build exit 0; prettier --check clean on all changed files.
